subsystems.name: Nonlinear transmission line
subsystems.role: the amplifying medium: a long coplanar waveguide whose inductance rises with current, so it mixes microwave tones.
parts: disordered NbTiN or TiN film, tens of nanometres thick
narrow centre strip and ground planes

subsystems.name: Dispersion and phase-matching structure
subsystems.role: keeps the pump, signal and idle tones travelling at compatible speeds so gain stays broadband instead of peaking.

subsystems.name: Pump and bias network
subsystems.role: injects the strong pump tone that supplies the energy for amplification and sets gain and saturation power.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic package
subsystems.role: holds the chip at millikelvin temperatures and anchors every incoming line so stray heat never reaches the device.
parts: thermal straps to the mixing-chamber plate

subsystems.name: Readout chain
subsystems.role: routes the amplified signal out without letting noise travel back into the quantum device.

subsystems.name: Noise and gain metrology
subsystems.role: proves that added noise really is close to the quantum limit and that gain is flat across the band.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the film
buildSteps.detail: Sputter a thin film of niobium titanium nitride or titanium nitride onto a high-resistivity silicon or sapphire wafer. Disordered growth is deliberate: it lowers the superfluid density and raises the kinetic inductance, which is the source of the nonlinearity.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the waveguide
buildSteps.detail: Optical or electron-beam lithography and etching define a coplanar waveguide with a narrow centre strip. Hundreds of millimetres of line are folded into a chip only a few millimetres across, because the gain grows with length.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the dispersion
buildSteps.detail: Periodic capacitors or resonant sections are patterned along the line in the same step. They slow the pump relative to signal and idle so the four-wave-mixing process stays phase-matched over gigahertz of bandwidth.

buildSteps.title: Package and thermalise
buildSteps.detail: The chip is mounted in a shielded box, wire-bonded to microwave connectors, and every input line is fitted with attenuators and thermal anchors so that room-temperature noise is absorbed before it reaches the device.

buildSteps.title: Cool to millikelvin
buildSteps.detail: The package is bolted to the mixing chamber of a dilution refrigerator and cooled to roughly ten to twenty millikelvin, the regime where added noise can approach the quantum limit.

buildSteps.title: Characterise gain and noise
buildSteps.detail: A pump tone is applied and swept in power and frequency while transmission, gain (typically around twenty decibels), bandwidth and saturation power are measured, then added noise is calibrated against a known reference.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into a system
buildSteps.detail: The amplifier is inserted into a real readout or receiver chain behind circulators and a 4 K transistor stage, and its ability to read many resonators or qubits through one cable is demonstrated.

prerequisites.why: niobium titanium nitride and titanium nitride give the high kinetic inductance and the current-dependent nonlinearity the whole device depends on.
millikelvin temperatures are needed for the added noise to fall near the quantum limit and for the films to stay superconducting with low loss.

prerequisites.tech: Microwave lithography for long low-loss lines
prerequisites.why: the transmission line must be metres of path length yet fit on a chip and lose almost nothing.
without them, amplified noise and the pump leak back into the qubits or detectors being read out.
measuring an added noise of a few hundred millikelvin at gigahertz frequencies is itself hard and needs careful cross-checks.

pathway.milestone: lab instruments reading out superconducting qubits and serving as the first amplifier in axion and dark-matter haloscopes
pathway.unlocks: broadband, near-quantum-limited sensing in magnetic fields where junction-based amplifiers fail.

pathway.milestone: routine replacement of Josephson-junction parametric amplifiers in multi-qubit readout chains
pathway.unlocks: one amplifier covering several gigahertz, so many qubits or resonators share a single cable and one set of electronics.

pathway.milestone: on-chip integration of amplifier, multiplexing and cryogenic control electronics
pathway.unlocks: scaling readout to thousands of qubits without a matching explosion in wiring and heat load.

pathway.milestone: materials and designs that work at higher temperatures, plus use as a standard component in quantum and dark-matter instruments
pathway.unlocks: simpler, cheaper cryogenics and wider adoption outside specialist laboratories.
